The axe murder incident was the killing of two United States Army officers by North Korean soldiers on August 18, 1976, in the Joint Security Area (JSA) located in the Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ). The officers had been part of a work party cutting down a poplar tree in the JSA that partially blocked the view of United Nations (U.N.) observers, when they were attacked by the North Koreans and killed.

In the JSA, near the Bridge of No Return, a 100-foot (30 m) poplar tree blocked the line of sight between a United Nations Command (UNC) checkpoint (CP No. 3) and an observation post (OP No. 5). This caused security concerns as the North Korean Army (KPA) had made numerous attempts to grab UNC personnel from CP No. 3 and drag them across the bridge into North Korean territory.

On August 18, 1976, a group of 19 American, South Korean and UN soldiers went into the JSA to trim the tree. The two captains did not wear side arms, as members of the JSA were limited to only five armed officers and 30 armed enlisted personnel at a time. However, there were axes in the back of their truck.

As trimming began, about 15 North Korean soldiers appeared and ordered a halt to the trimming, claiming that "Kim Il Sung personally planted it and nourished it and it's growing under his supervision."

After being ignored, 20 more North Koreans arrived carrying crowbars and clubs and were ordered to attack. The entire fight lasted for only 20–30 seconds before the UNC force managed to disperse the North Koreans. One killed soldier was retrieved but another could not be found. OP No. 5 observed that a North Korean soldier was taking an axe down into a depression for a couple of minutes, then coming back up and handing the axe to another guard who would repeat the process. That was reported to OP No. 3 who sent a search and rescue party and recovered the body of another American soldier.

In response, the UNC determined that instead of trimming the branches that obscured visibility, they would cut down the tree with overwhelming force and three days later launched Operation Paul Bunyon, which involved over 813 soldiers, several helicopters, fighter jets and B-52 bombers. Five minutes into the operation, the UNC notified their North Korean counterparts at the JSA that a UN work party had entered the JSA "in order to peacefully finish the work left unfinished" on August 18 and the operation concluded peacefully.

This came up as a response in another thread. I thought it might be worth sharing. This list gives you different "tools". Each type of gun serves a different purpose. Opinions on firearms are usually not in short supply, so if yours if different or you think mine sucks let me know.

  • Shotgun - Birds, home defense, deer hunting in some states, and skeet shooting. I recommend getting a two barrel combo.

  • 22LR or .17 HMR Rifle - Small game, cheap target practice.

  • Two primary pistols - One which can be used for home defense and secondary open carry. Another smaller pistol for concealed carry (I use a G17 and G26). Pistols are a personal preference. I like the 9mm Glocks, but there is going to be a huge amount of opinions on which pistols are "best" usually it boils down to preference.

  • 22LR Pistol - I like having this as a target pistol. It is also much more compact to take with you than a rifle and is still accurate enough to hunt small game.

  • Hunting Rifle - Like pistols there is going to be a huge amount of opinions on this. The 30-06, .270, and .308 calibers all being popular choices.

  • GET OFF MY Lawn - Zombie Apocalypse Rifle - AR-15, AK 74, or AK 47. When you want to put a lot of lead down range fast, this is your go to.
Guns are tools. Do you have the right tool for the job?

They're considered specialty rounds and good luck finding them. The 12 gauge is the most popular, followed by the 20 ga, the the 410. The 410 is only good for small game and target shooting. The 20 gauge will have less recoil than the 12, mostly because of smaller shells. This is the best choice if you want something smaller that the 12. The 410 will be harder to find a variety of ammo for, but you can still find it.
